mechanism_narrative: The sharp one-week rise in PARKS mobility from -6.7 to +1.7 signals a surge in outdoor leisure activity that spills over into nearby retail and recreation venues, causing RETAIL_REC to rise over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days despite PARKS remaining above 0 for the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in WORKPLACES mobility of more than 8 points week-on-week (from -4.4 to -13.1) signals a sudden shift to remote work or holidays, removing weekday commuter footfall from retail districts and depressing RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 8 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days when WORKPLACES falls more than 8 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT mobility falls below -10 and RESIDENTIAL mobility exceeds 10, residents stay local and avoid central shopping districts, reducing aggregate RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -10 and RESIDENTIAL exceeds 10
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days when TRANSIT is below -10 and RESIDENTIAL is above 10.

mechanism_narrative: In the summer holiday season, high PARKS mobility (>0) combined with low WORKPLACES mobility (<-10) indicates leisure-oriented trips that boost retail and recreation spending, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days despite PARKS >0 and WORKPLACES < -10 at the decision point.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM mobility rises above -2, it signals a renewed focus on necessity shopping that crowds out discretionary retail trips, causing RETAIL_REC to fall over the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days when GROCERY_PHARM exceeds -2.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated RESIDENTIAL mobility above 10 indicates that people are spending more time at home, reducing trips to retail and recreation venues and driving RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL mobility remaining above 10 for the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of PARKS mobility above 0 and TRANSIT mobility below -13 signals a shift toward local outdoor leisure and away from long-distance retail trips, which increases local retail footfall and raises RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days when PARKS > 0 and TRANSIT < -13.

mechanism_narrative: The recent stabilization of RETAIL_REC combined with improving GROCERY_PHARM mobility (rising above -4) signals growing consumer confidence to resume discretionary spending, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days when GROCERY_PHARM is above -4 at the decision point.
